item.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen Model for Enhanced Search Performance
item.description:
Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen Model for Enhanced Search Performance

Google has released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new model designed to provide more helpful answers to complex queries, including multi-part questions, highly specific requests, and those containing hard-to-understand typos. According to Google, the model can break down questions and address each individual part in its responses. Robby Stein, VP of product at Google Search, says the update is now the default model in AI Mode and is being used for difficult questions in AI Overviews.

🔍 Overview

Google says the new model delivers significant leaps in both speed and intelligence compared to Gemini Flash 3.8. Stein describes Gemini 4 Hydrogen as “the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.” The model’s performance reportedly matches or outperforms competing models in its class, such as Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Terra.

🧩 How it works

To improve information retrieval and language understanding, the model employs several new processing techniques:

  • Simultaneous Queries: The model conducts simultaneous queries across all relevant subtopics to provide a wider range of links in its responses.
  • Improved Language Understanding: Understanding has been improved across all supported AI Mode languages.
  • Breakdown Capability: The model addresses complex questions by breaking them down and responding to each component.

⚙️ Key details

Responses from Gemini 4 Hydrogen now feature a broader range of visuals, including images, comparison tables, graphs, and maps. In one example provided by Stein, the AI generated an interactive animated driving simulation to explain how phones locate specific highway lanes in areas without cell service.

Users are also provided with expanded thinking level options:

  • Low
  • Medium
  • High
  • xhigh (New)

🚀 Availability

Starting today, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is available in the following products and services:

  • Google Search and the Gemini app
  • All tiers of Google AI Studio and the Gemini API
  • Gemini for business
  • Google Antigravity (available for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers)

#Google #Gemini #ArtificialIntelligence #Search #Gemini4Hydrogen

Source: Google’s new Gemini model is better at understanding complicated questions

item.title: Midterm Election Shifts AI Landscape Amid Big Tech Loss and Monetization Uncertainty
item.description:
Midterm Election Shifts AI Landscape Amid Big Tech Loss and Monetization Uncertainty

On Tuesday, millions of American voters went to the polls and voted overwhelmingly for Democrats and against AI. The results have major implications for the technology sector, especially AI development and data‑center investments.

🗳️ Election Outcome

  • “On Tuesday, millions of American voters went to the polls and voted overwhelmingly for Democrats and against AI.”
  • “Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election”

🏗️ Data‑Center Fight

  • “The fight against Big Tech is about to come roaring back, and the fight over data centers is looking even harder for the folks trying to build them.”

📻 The Vergecast Takeaways

  • “On The Vergecast: blue waves, the confusing business of AI search, and the many thoughts of RAM Altman.”
  • “On this episode of The Vergecast, Nilay and David discuss what the 2026 midterms mean for the tech industry going forward.”
  • “They dig into the self-quarantining echo chamber that is X, the congressional energy likely to be pointed at tech CEOs and AI regulation, and whether anything is actually likely to get done in the next two years.”
  • “After that, the hosts turn to AI.”

💰 AI Monetization Questions

  • “Specifically, whether anyone has figured out how to make money on AI.”
  • “Specifically, whether OpenAI’s explosive growth in web search means much, when even Google can’t figure out how to make money on AI web search.”
  • “Businesses are scaling back; agents don’t appear to be taking over.”
  • “There’s a lot of money flowing around the AI world, but is there enough flowing into it to keep everything going?”
  • “That’s the hard part.”

📈 Outlook

The conversation highlights a growing uncertainty: while AI continues to attract capital, questions about sustainable revenue models and the ability to expand critical infrastructure such as data centers remain unanswered.

#AI #Election2026 #BigTech #WebSearch #AIRevenue

Source: Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election

item.title: Google’s AI‑Mode Search Boosts Queries but Slows Ad Revenue Growth
item.description:
Google’s AI‑Mode Search Boosts Queries but Slows Ad Revenue Growth

Google reported that search queries are growing at their fastest rate in five years, but the monetization of those queries is lagging as the company rolls out AI‑Mode.

📈 Search Growth vs. Revenue

  • Queries are up at the fastest pace in five years, according to Alphabet’s earnings report.
  • Search revenue growth slowed to 12 % YoY in Q3, down from roughly 17 % in the prior quarter.
  • Growth in paid clicks fell from 13 % to 8 %.
Metric Q3 YoY Prior Quarter
Search revenue growth 12 % ~17 %
Paid‑click growth 8 % 13 %

🤖 AI‑Mode Impact

  • AI‑Mode queries are growing strongly but are monetizing at a lower rate than traditional searches.
  • Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler says most AI‑Mode queries are “incremental” – additional questions rather than replacements for existing searches.
  • Many AI‑Mode queries are upper‑funnel, meaning users are researching potential purchases before they know exactly what they want.
  • Google is expanding ads in AI Overviews and AI‑Mode internationally and across multiple turns of U.S. AI‑Mode conversations.
  • The company has floated bringing ads to its standalone Gemini app, leveraging formats developed for AI‑Mode, though no timeline has been announced.

💰 Financial Reaction

  • Alphabet’s shares have fallen about 14 % since the earnings report, as investors question the costs and returns of the company’s AI ambitions.
  • Alphabet plans to spend roughly $200 billion this year on infrastructure, largely to support AI.
  • Schindler cites currency effects and changing advertiser spending in specific industries as the biggest drivers of the slowdown.

📊 Advertiser Perspective

  • Tinuiti’s same‑store advertisers increased Google paid‑search spending 14 % YoY in Q3 while maintaining their return‑on‑ad‑spend targets.
  • Andy Taylor (Tinuiti) notes, “We’re still seeing a good return, and we’re not seeing performance take a hit.”
  • However, Google does not let advertisers separately target AI‑Mode inventory or break out its performance.
  • “If people are clicking through less often, that is a challenge that they need to figure out,” says an industry representative.

🛠️ Analyst Views & Open Questions

  • Nate Elliott (eMarketer) calls this “the first major disruption that Google is facing to its core business in decades.”
  • Elliott adds, “It’s not a slam dunk that it’s going to turn into more effective advertising.”
  • An October working paper found that U.S. visits from ChatGPT ads generated 64 % less revenue per session for retailers than visits from Google Search ads ($0.89 vs. $2.45). The paper measures retailer sales, not platform revenue, and does not establish how Google’s own AI ads perform.
  • Both Google and competitors like OpenAI are still figuring out how to make ads work in AI contexts—delivering results for advertisers while keeping users satisfied.

🔍 Why It Matters

  • AI is reshaping how people find information and whether they click on the ads that fund Google’s business.
  • The shift toward AI‑Mode could alter the balance between query volume growth and ad revenue, influencing Google’s long‑term profitability and the broader digital‑advertising ecosystem.

#Google #AI #Advertising #Search

Source: Google hasn’t figured out how to make AI pay like its search engine

item.title: OpenAI says ChatGPT handles 20% of Google’s search query volume
item.description:
OpenAI says ChatGPT handles 20% of Google’s search query volume

In many circles, “Ask Chat” has replaced “Google it,” and that’s reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google.

🔍 Overview

  • “OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search”
  • “ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI.”
  • The announcement was made by Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, at a press event on Monday.

🧩 Definition of Search

  • Fry said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how‑to explanation.

⚙️ Key Details

  • The reported volume is one‑fifth of Google’s search traffic.
  • “Having one-fifth as many searches as Google is still a long way from overtaking it, but for comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google’s 2023 antitrust trial that Bing had about 3 percent of the search engine market share after trying for more than a decade.”
  • OpenAI likely uses Microsoft Bing for a significant part of its searches, along with its in‑house search index, although there is still speculation that some queries are routed through Google.
  • “During the trial, Google described AI as a potential disruptor, arguing ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it — now, OpenAI seems to agree.”

💰 Monetization

  • “Much like Google, OpenAI sees a potential path to profitability through ads, particularly as it approaches an IPO potentially slated for early next year.”
  • “OpenAI announced last month that the company would begin introducing images of sponsored products and services in ChatGPT rather than just a company’s name, logo, and a link to its product like before.”
  • “Ads have not negatively impacted the product or the usage of the product,” Fry said, adding that “most people do not seem to mind ads in the product.”
  • “Ads have maybe shown us that we could be doing this more, actually,” Fry said.

📊 Competitive Landscape

  • Google continues to reduce conventional referrals to third‑party sites and invests heavily in AI tools, including personalized search results with visualizations and charts.
  • Other companies are investing in AI‑focused search experiences; for OpenAI, it’s called “Intelligent UI,” a visual and interactive interface within a chatbot response.

🚀 Future Direction

  • Fry described the vision: “That’s where the future of this technology goes. You’re talking to a canvas,” he said.
  • OpenAI’s focus on an “Intelligent UI” suggests a shift toward a more visual, interactive search experience embedded in chat.

#OpenAI #ChatGPT #Search #Ads #AI

Source: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search

item.title: Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode Reduce Publisher Traffic
item.description:
Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode Reduce Publisher Traffic

Publishers spent years figuring out how to get clicks on Google, building a reciprocal relationship where they supplied content and Google supplied exposure. In 2024 and 2025 Google introduced AI‑driven search features that have reshaped that relationship and sharply lowered traffic to many news sites.

🔍 Overview

  • AI Overviews (2024) – An AI‑generated summary appears at the very top of Google Search, followed by links to sources the AI deems most useful. [Evidence]
  • AI Mode (May 2025) – Replaces standard search with a chatbot‑like interface that provides detailed summaries from web results. [Evidence]
  • The features change how results are ranked and displayed, making it harder for publishers to rely on Google traffic alone. [Evidence]

🗓️ Timeline

Year Feature Key Change
2024 AI Overviews AI‑generated summary placed at top of results with source links below.
2025 AI Mode Standard search replaced by a chatbot‑style interface that returns detailed summaries.

📉 Impact on Publishers

  • News outlets that spent time and money optimizing pages for clicks saw traffic tank after the AI features launched. [Evidence]
  • The Wall Street Journal (June 2025) reported declines for Business Insider, The Washington Post, HuffPost, and the WSJ itself since 2022. [Evidence]
  • Similarweb data showed The New York Times’ search traffic fell from 44 % to 35.5 % over three years. [Evidence]
  • DCN reported 19 members lost 1–25 % of Google traffic between May and June 2025. [Evidence]
  • DMG Media (Daily Mail, Metro) told the UK CMA click‑through rates dropped up to 89 % between June and July 2025, citing AI Overviews. [Evidence]
  • Pew Research found users are less likely to click on external links when an AI Overview is shown. [Evidence]
  • The News/Media Alliance warned AI Overviews would be “catastrophic” for web traffic. [Evidence]

🛠️ Google’s Response

  • Offered a toggle that lets sites opt out of appearing in AI Overviews and AI Mode without losing standard search visibility (rolled out after a UK order). [Evidence]
  • Made source links more prominent: hovering over a link shows a pop‑up with article titles and images. [Evidence]
  • Added another AI change that puts in‑line links higher up in responses more frequently. [Evidence]
  • Google’s leadership statements: Liz Reid said click volume remained “relatively stable,” while Nick Fox said “from our point of view, the web is thriving.” [Evidence]

⚖️ Legal and Regulatory Context

  • US District Judge Amit Mehta dismissed an antitrust suit from Chegg and Penske Media and rejected a class‑action claim from Arkansas newspapers over AI Overviews. [Evidence]
  • The UK Competition and Markets Authority received complaints from DMG Media about click‑through declines linked to AI Overviews. [Evidence]

The rollout of AI Overviews and AI Mode marks a significant shift in Google Search, turning a long‑standing traffic source into a more opaque AI‑mediated layer and prompting measurable traffic losses across the digital publishing ecosystem.

#GoogleAI #DigitalPublishing #SearchTraffic #AIOverviews

Source: Google’s AI search changes upended online publishing

item.title: Judge Dismisses Chegg and PMC Antitrust Lawsuits Over Google AI Search
item.description:
Judge Dismisses Chegg and PMC Antitrust Lawsuits Over Google AI Search

Federal Judge Amit Mehta dismissed the antitrust lawsuits brought by Chegg and Rolling Stone parent Penske Media Corporation, which alleged that Google’s AI‑powered search features siphoned traffic from their sites.

🔍 Overview

  • Chegg and PMC claimed Google abused monopoly power by coercing publishers into providing content for AI Overviews for free, or risk disappearing from search results.
  • The lawsuits, filed last year, asserted that Google’s AI search features diverted traffic away from publishers, hurting revenue.

⚖️ Legal Ruling

  • Judge Mehta wrote that the plaintiffs’ claims “don’t stand up to antitrust law.”
  • He noted the plaintiffs have only “pleaded an ‘expectation’ that Google will send them search traffic if they make their content available for free.”
  • “But an expectation is not an agreement. It is simply how a general search engine works,” Mehta wrote.
  • The court is “not ‘unsympathetic to the situation publishers now find themselves in,’” but said antitrust rules cannot replace legislative action on the economic impact of “new innovation.”

📉 Impact on Publishers

  • Publishers continue to see a steep dive in traffic to news outlets and small websites after Google’s AI‑powered search overhaul.

💰 Google Pilot Payments

  • This week, The Information reported that Google is paying around 100 publishers for their contributions to AI Overviews, AI Mode, and Gemini as part of a pilot program.

Disclosure: The Verge is part of Penske Media.

#Google #Antitrust #AIOverviews

Source: Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews

item.title: Google Launches Pilot Program to Pay Publishers for AI Contributions
item.description:
Google Launches Pilot Program to Pay Publishers for AI Contributions

Google has introduced a pilot program that compensates publishers for their contributions to its AI-powered search features and chatbot, according to reports from Digiday and The Information.

⚙️ Key details

  • The program began less than a year ago.
  • Approximately 100 publishers have joined the pilot.
  • Payments are based on how much content contributed to:
    • AI Overviews
    • AI Mode in Search
    • Gemini chatbot

💰 Compensation Examples

Publisher Status Reported Earnings
Joined at program start Over $1 million in a year
Joined a few months ago Around $50,000 to $60,000

💡 Why it matters

Google is facing scrutiny regarding the impact of its AI features on web traffic. This comes alongside regulatory actions:

  • In June, the UK ruled that Google must allow publishers to opt out of appearing in AI search features.
  • The European Union has opened an investigation into the impact on web traffic and ordered Google to make changes to its search engine.

#Google #AI #Publishing #Gemini #Search

Source: Google reportedly tests paying publishers for AI search results
